question.text: Under the Companies Act 2013, a company-structured AIF is limited to making private placements to a maximum of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Companies are restricted under the Companies Act 2013 to making private placements to not more than 200 investors. AIF Regulations permit up to 1,000 investors per scheme, so the company structure is more restrictive than the AIF scheme cap (p. 104). The Trap: The 200-investor private-placement limit under the Companies Act is lower than the AIF 1,000-investor scheme limit. Treating the 200 limit as halving capacity versus a trust structure is not arithmetically correct; the relevant comparison is with the 1,000-investor AIF scheme cap. Note: Company structure is more restrictive than the AIF 1,000-investor scheme limit; choose between structures with that comparison in mind rather than informal halving rules.
